title: Typestate Neglect (Temporal Coupling Panic)
pattern: Methods must be called in a strict chronological sequence, but they are declared on a single public struct, relying on runtime checks and panics to enforce call order.
why_bad: It introduces temporal coupling that is hidden from the compiler. Another programmer can easily call the methods out of order, leading to avoidable runtime panics or silent logic bugs.
detection: A method that panics or returns an error if a boolean state flag has not been set by a previous method call on the same struct.
counterexample: Event loops or stream processes where the order of incoming external events is inherently unpredictable.
fix: Use the **Typestate pattern** in Rust: design methods to consume the struct and return a new distinct type representing the next state, ensuring compile-time order.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 17, G31 ("Hidden Temporal Coupling"); Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 13.
